attempts.url: AWS publishes no OpenAPI document for S3; its own machine spec is the SDK service model

attempts.note: AWS's own service model in the legacy SDK v2 JSON format. Rejected on 2026-09-03 for want of a converter; superseded on 2026-11-16 by the Smithy form of the same model, which src/smithy.ts converts
apis.guru's aws2openapi rendering of the AWS model: third-party and frozen at about 2021 (97 operations). Used from 2026-09-03 until 2026-11-16, then superseded by AWS's own model

AWS's own Smithy JSON AST for S3, from the AWS-owned github.com/aws/api-models-aws repository (README: Smithy models for all public AWS API services; NOTICE: Copyright Amazon.com, Inc.). The jsDelivr mirror https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/aws/api-models-aws@main/models/s3/service/2006-03-01/s3-2006-03-01.json returned byte-identical content

notes: Full coverage of the Amazon S3 REST API (2006-03-01), converted by src/smithy.ts from AWS's own Smithy service model, saved verbatim as upstream.json. COUNTS: the model has 112 operations, all bound with smithy.api#http, and openapi.json has 112 operations over 59 path keys; none were skipped and the converter raised no warnings. The model has 710 data shapes; openapi.json has 559 component schemas: 529 shapes carried as they are, plus 30 body schemas for operation inputs/outputs that have an XML body. The other 151 operation input/output structures have no schema of their own because every member is a path, query or header parameter, a response header or a raw payload. DIFF against the apis.guru rendering this replaces (97 operations, 574 schemas): 19 operations added (CreateSession, ListDirectoryBuckets, RenameObject, UpdateObjectEncryption, GetBucketAbac, PutBucketAbac, the four object-annotation operations and the nine bucket metadata-configuration operations) and 4 removed, the legacy GetBucketLifecycle, PutBucketLifecycle, GetBucketNotification and PutBucketNotification, which AWS's current model no longer declares. Those four shared their request URI with the current GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, GetBucketNotificationConfiguration and PutBucketNotificationConfiguration (GET/PUT /{Bucket}?lifecycle and ?notification), so no URL is lost. 13 path keys changed spelling for the same operationId (for example GET / is now GET /#x-id=ListBuckets because ListDirectoryBuckets shares that URI, and PUT /{Bucket}#analytics&id is now PUT /{Bucket}#analytics). ADAPTOR SURFACE: @openfn/language-aws-s3 1.1.4 exposes put, list and get, which send PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command and GetObjectCommand; PutObject (PUT /{Bucket}/{Key}), ListObjectsV2 (GET /{Bucket}#list-type=2) and GetObject (GET /{Bucket}/{Key}) are all present. PATH KEYS: operations that share a method and path are told apart by a # fragment carrying the URI's literal query (#acl, #list-type=2), then required query parameters (#uploadId), then required headers (#x-amz-copy-source). The SDK-only x-id hint is kept as an optional query parameter and used in a key only for ListBuckets and ListDirectoryBuckets. GROUPING: the model declares no resources, so the 15 endpoints.md groups come from a tag table in src/smithy.ts (was 3 path-derived groups). MODELLED LOOSELY: paths are path-style (/{Bucket}/...) on https://s3.{region}.amazonaws.com, while real clients mostly use virtual-hosted hosts resolved by endpoint rules that are not carried; {Key+} is written {Key}, so the conformer does not match a key that contains a slash (also true of the previous spec); XML bodies are JSON-Schema objects under application/xml with xml.name/attribute/wrapped where the model states them, not a full XML binding; object bodies are binary application/octet-stream; SelectObjectContent's event stream is a schema under application/vnd.amazon.eventstream, not a framed stream; x-amz-meta-* prefix headers are one header named x-amz-meta-*; SigV4 is declared as an Authorization apiKey scheme; only the errors the model lists per operation are documented (20 operations), and an error with no httpError (NotFound) takes Smithy's default of 400 although S3 answers 404; smithy.api#examples, waiters and checksum traits are not carried. Descriptions keep AWS's HTML.
